newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds stay up in quiet market, focus on US.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds stay up in quiet market, focus on US.

text.p: Danish bond prices slipped a little after early advances in a quiet, yet positive holiday market on Friday with focus on the upcoming June U.S. PPI data.

"The market has been quieter than in previous days with focus on short-term paper. We dipped a little after early gains because of Britain's rate hike. The undertone is positive, good U.S. figures should spark fresh gains," one dealer said.

The tone-setting eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.05 point from the start at 113.87, yielding 5.90 percent, while the seven percent 2007 forthcoming benchmark was up by the same margin at 106.63, with 6.11 percent yield.

Turnover in the 2006 benchmark was 800 million crowns with the 2007 at 500 million crowns. The 2006's September future rose 0.18 point to 113.22 with 25 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.18 point to 92.33.
The crown traded at 3.8098 per mark at 1135 GMT, up from around 3.8100 at the opening.

The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 56 basis points. The Central Bank was active on the market selling 100 million crowns worth of the seven percent 2007 bond as part of its routine financing operations.
